front: Array vs. Linked List: key runtime tradeoff?
back: Arrays give O(1) random access but O(n) insert/delete (must shift). Linked lists give O(1) insert/delete at a known position but O(n) random access.

front: Singly vs. doubly linked list: why does delete differ in complexity?
back: Singly linked lists lack a prev pointer, so deleting requires walking from head to find the predecessor — Θ(n). Doubly linked lists have prev, making delete Θ(1) given a pointer to the node.

front: What purpose does a sentinel (Wächter) node serve in a linked list?
back: It eliminates special-case handling for empty lists or list boundaries during insert/delete, since every real node always has a valid neighbor to link against.

front: What is the complexity of inserting at the head of a linked list?
back: Θ(1) — just repoint a couple of pointers, no shifting needed.

front: Remove all duplicates from an unsorted SINGLY-linked list, using only O(1) extra space (no hash set), non-recursively -- what's the achievable runtime, and why not better?
back: O(n^2). A singly-linked list can't look backward, so without extra memory to remember 'seen' values, each element must be checked against everything ahead of it -- there's no way to hash-dedupe in O(1) space.

front: RemoveDuplicates(L) on a singly linked list: what's the loop invariant for the outer while-loop (pointer a)?
back: Before the i-th outer iteration, the sublist from the head up to and including a contains no duplicates, and every occurrence of an already-visited node's key has been removed from the rest of the list.
